title: When the Kitchen Sings
premise: Marguerite Ravensworth inherited Bellhaven Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and she has learned to treat her heart like any other muscle: disciplined, contained, never overworked. When her family reunion threatens to expose how badly the estate is failing, she persuades Theo Marchetti, the ferry mechanic who once fixed her tractor and asks no questions, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, but Theo is hiding his own truth: his family holds the loan that could take Bellhaven. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Marguerite must choose between protecting her inheritance and trusting a man whose loyalty to his family may cost her everything — and in the end, she risks the whole heart, signing away part of the vineyard to save both their families and choosing love over duty as the ferry sounds its final horn.
about_author: Elodie Halloran spent a decade working seasonal jobs on coastal farms and ferries before turning her notebooks of overheard confessions into romance novels. She writes from a drafty cottage overlooking a harbor, where she insists the best love stories begin with someone pretending not to look.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She walks the half-harvested rows of Bellhaven Vineyard, tallying what the bank letter means against what the land once meant to her grandmother. A call from her aunt confirms the family reunion will happen at the estate whether she likes it or not. Emotional beat: weary defiance masking fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixes Things
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The tractor dies during pressing week, and Theo Marchetti, the ferry mechanic who takes odd jobs off-season, arrives with grease on his knuckles and an unnerving habit of listening more than he talks. She catches herself laughing for the first time in months. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth.

chapters.title: An Invitation She Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her aunt phones: cousins are bringing spouses, the family expects news of Marguerite's 'settling down,' and failure at love will be read as failure at life. Staring at the reunion invitation, she invents a boyfriend on the spot. Emotional beat: panic sharpening into recklessness.

chapters.title: A Favor, Priced in Dinners
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marguerite asks him to be her fake date; he refuses twice, then sees the eviction notice tucked in her ledger and agrees — for home-cooked dinners through winter. He tells himself it's charity. It isn't. Emotional beat: self-deception beginning.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Over wine and index cards they build a history: first date at the lighthouse, three months together, his job at the marina. Every invented detail feels dangerously easy, and Marguerite notices she's memorizing his real answers too. Emotional beat: intimacy disguised as rehearsal.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Dawn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They cross to the mainland for the reunion, and Theo watches Marguerite armor herself as the shoreline approaches. He learns she hums when nervous — the same tune the kitchen radio plays. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Arrival at Ravensworth House
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The family descends: her imperious aunt Vivienne, golden-boy cousin Charles, and sharp-eyed Grandmother Iris, who greets Theo with a look that says she knows exactly what this is. The performance begins at the door. Emotional beat: stage fright and spite.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At dinner, under interrogation about their courtship, Theo improvises a story so specific and kind that Marguerite forgets it's fiction. Their hands meet under the table and neither pulls away. Emotional beat: the lie turning true.

chapters.title: What Iris Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Grandmother Iris corners him alone and reveals she recognizes his surname — Marchetti — the family that holds Bellhaven's debt. She offers him money to walk away and spare Marguerite humiliation. He refuses, unsettled. Emotional beat: loyalty versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Kitchen Sings
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Unable to sleep, she finds Theo baking bread in the estate kitchen at midnight, flour everywhere, radio playing. They dance badly between counters and almost kiss — interrupted by a cousin. Emotional beat: desire breaking through containment.

chapters.title: Sunday Confessions
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The reunion ends in near-disaster when Charles announces the vineyard's insolvency to the whole table. Marguerite defends herself fiercely, and Theo stands beside her, unasked. Driving home, she realizes she isn't performing anymore. Emotional beat: solidarity becoming love.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back home, Theo's father demands he deliver the foreclosure notice personally — a test of family loyalty. Theo hides the letter instead, lying to both households now. Emotional beat: guilt compounding like interest.

chapters.title: Harvest Without a Plan
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite throws herself into an impossible harvest to prove the vineyard viable, and Theo works beside her every day, unpaid. Her aunt warns her that men who work for free want something. Emotional beat: hope entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Vines
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A storm threatens the crop; they fight side by side through the night to save it, soaked and laughing and finally kissing in the barn afterward. Theo nearly confesses everything. He doesn't. Emotional beat: peak happiness built on a fault line.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Iris sends Marguerite an old photograph: Theo's father signing the loan papers years ago, with young Theo in the background. Marguerite confronts Theo, who admits only that his family lent the money — not that the notice exists. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold wind.

chapters.title: Loyalty Versus Truth
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father discovers the hidden foreclosure letter and delivers it himself, publicly, at the vineyard gate. Marguerite learns Theo knew for weeks. She tells him to leave. Emotional beat: heartbreak as arithmetic — trust divided by silence equals zero.

chapters.title: Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Alone, Marguerite bakes the bread Theo taught her and burns it, then sits in the dark kitchen understanding that she taught herself not to need anyone long before he lied. Aunt Vivienne offers to buy the debt and control the estate. Emotional beat: grief clarifying into resolve.

chapters.title: The Son Who Says No
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his father: the loan was vengeance from an old feud, not business, and foreclosing destroys two families to settle one man's pride. His father disowns the argument; Theo walks out, taking the original loan documents with him. Emotional beat: severing duty to claim truth.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Theo returns with the documents and a proposal: restructure the debt using his savings and the vineyard's next vintage, with Marguerite keeping majority control. She must decide whether love that began as a lie can be trusted with her inheritance. Emotional beat: risk weighed in full.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the dock, as the last autumn ferry prepares to depart — with Theo supposedly aboard it back to his old life — Marguerite runs the length of the pier and stops him. She offers not pieces of her heart but all of it, debts included. Emotional beat: the leap.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Spring: the restructured vineyard's first joint harvest begins, Iris approves of Theo with terrifying warmth, and the kitchen radio plays while two families learn to share a table. The bread rises perfectly. Emotional beat: earned peace.

chapters.title: When the Kitchen Sings
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. One year later, Marguerite and Theo host the family reunion themselves, serving wine from vines everyone said were dead. Asked how they met, they tell the truth: a fake date that became real by dessert. Emotional beat: joy that no longer needs containing.
